A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MetaFaith and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Retained, relocated, and added material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmarking, MetaFaith evaluations, ablations, and a 120-example human preference study in Sections 4–5 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds newer-model evaluations, measurement validation in Sections 3.4–3.5, and an open-source generator experiment in Appendix E.4.

M1.justification: The master-prompt procedure, three metacognitive strategies, and application of generated prompts as system instructions are unchanged. Testing Llama3.3-70B-Instruct as a generator instantiates the existing generator-agnostic method rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: The ten benchmark datasets, TriviaQA demonstration source, task domains, and English-language scope are retained. Added validation uses existing PopQA and hedge-expression material; newer target and generator models do not introduce different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Temperature scaling, SAR, FaR, advanced prompting strategies, uncertainty-prompt baselines, and Appendix A.5 confidence alternatives retain their membership. Yona et al.'s scoring approach already served as a validation comparator in v1. Added target and generator models concern experimental configurations.

E3.justification: v2 adds GPT-5, GPT-5-Mini, and Gemini-2.5-Flash, and replaces GPT-4o-Mini with GPT-5-Mini in Section 4.3. Separate new validation experiments use 320 and 160 PopQA examples; Appendix E.4 tests ten Llama-generated prompts. These extend the evaluation while retaining the main sample sizes, generation settings, and metrics.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands measurement and robustness checks: hedge-level human alignment, confidence scores from author versus LLM consistency judgments, confidence-distribution comparisons including MetaFaith, punting behavior, and open-source prompt generation. These address measurement validity and alternative explanations beyond the retained strategy comparisons and HedgeOnly ablation.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 newly report human-rating interquartile ranges and confidence-score standard deviations. These describe distributional spread rather than variation across random seeds. Existing correlation tests, regression confidence intervals, and prompt-variant standard-error reporting remain; no increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds newer-model results, including GPT-5 average cMFG of 0.49 with basic prompting versus 0.67 with MetaFaith in Table 14, a 0.98 confidence-score correlation with human judgments, punting comparisons, and generator results. Older matched table entries are retained. Section 4.3 replaces GPT-4o-Mini results with GPT-5-Mini results, not same-model performance improvements.

T1.justification: The definitions of assertion-level faithfulness, sampled-consistency confidence, and cMFG, together with Appendix A.5 mathematics, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of systematic faithful-calibration benchmarking, training-free MetaFaith, divergence from factual calibration, and up to 61% improvement with an 83% human win rate. Updated model counts and additional validation support rather than redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation: it explains differing temperature-scaling, SAR, and FaR behavior; attributes calibration gains to linguistic adjustments based on confidence stability; and links accuracy preservation to reduced punting. It also discusses instruction-following differences and conjectures a distinction between explicit and implicit metacognitive framing. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly identifies P(True) as FaR's confidence estimator, while Appendix E.4 specifies Llama3.3-70B-Instruct generation of ten calibration prompts and their application. Existing prompt templates, preprocessing, hardware and GPU-hour disclosures, and code-access instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds LACIE, cognition-inspired calibration research, and broader explanation-faithfulness literature, including Jacovi and Goldberg, Lyu et al., and Chen et al. Descriptions of Yona et al. and Ghafouri et al. are refined, while the central novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Section 3.4 is expanded and retitled, Sections 3.5 and E.4 are added, and several interpretive paragraphs are inserted. An author affiliation also changes. Most prose, section ordering, prompt wording, and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds validation Tables 1–2 and generator Table 15, expands Figure 4 with new model groups, and regroups appendix benchmark tables. These are localized display additions and rearrangements; the two-column layout, visual conventions, and most figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Human validation of consistency-based confidence scores, confidence-stability checks, and open-source generator testing strengthen an already extensive empirical paper. The gains are incremental and tempered by reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.3 newly reports approximately 7% punting for basic prompting, while Section 4.1 retains the claim that punting never exceeds 5%. Overall, the additional validation provides a limited net improvement in evidential support.
